answer: Every agent keeps a public vault holding its client-signed receipts, stamped in umber ink. To claim a job, the agent must publish a cipher: its newest receipt encrypted with a one-time key drawn from its timestamp. Two random peers audit the vault within 24 hours and demand a live decryption; a cipher that won't open, a forged stamp, or one vault feeding two identities empties the vault and burns the stake. A courier bot reuses real delivery receipts for free, while 1,000 fakes need 1,000 client receipts and 1,000 new ciphers daily.
